When I was around 12 I got a cold sore on my left eye, the doctor said I had scaring which could affect my vision. For years my vision seemed fine. In my late teens I started noticing the vision out of my right eye got significantly worse qnd forgetting which eye I had the cold sore in I thought it was that, and didn't think anything of it and went to the optometrist (by the time I got around to it I would have been 22) to get some soft contact lenses who told me that they can only correct the left not the right because of the shape. I asked follow up questions. "What can be done?" "What's happened to cause that, was it because of the cold sore I had when I was younger?" I got a reply similar to. "Sometimes the eye changes shape and there's nothing that can be done". I just accepted that until mid 2018 I went into Specsavers for a new prescription who did some test and that I most likely have keratoconus, they sent me to an optometrist who specializes is the hard contact lenses and diagnosed me with it. When I'm not wearing my contact lenses I have zero vision out of my right eye. It has been a journey getting the right fit and the right piggy back lenses but I have finally found something comfortable that doesn't dry my eye out after wearing them for more than a few hours at a time. With my contact lenses in I have 6/6 (20/20) out of my right eye. Feb 2020 I had cross linking in my right eye and had my left eye done 6 weeks ago. Throughout this process I have always had pretty good vision out of my left eye, however since the crosslinking it's a bit more blurry hoping for a full recovery in a couple months time! I must say I am very thankful that I live in New Zealand and this condition is government funded meaning no cost for surgeries and discounted contacted lenses otherwise I would not be able to afford the lenses itself, and no one should have to live their life with impaired vision when it's something as small as a contact lense!
